AUTOMATIC_FINDINGS.md.previousSource:
# Stage 6 corrected results presentation

The focused UX correction supersedes the initial Stage 6 supplemental-only layout. `ResultsPresentation.select` chooses one primary result across original/manual/automatic/embedded evidence. `AutomaticUI` presents that result and concise supporting evidence; it does not manufacture matches. The later [stress correction](STAGE6_STRESS_REVIEW.md) makes one independently justified matching-policy change for complete reference-label sequences crossing the actual registrant boundary. Parsing, comparison schemas, reference storage, input datasets and pins remain unchanged; derived index policy/source metadata is regenerated under Deno 2.9.7.

Supported embedded comparisons to Expected Hostname, Personal Reference Domains and the original inspected hostname enter the same warning selection independently of built-in reference membership or eligibility. Only verified visual proof or a complete comparison name inside a different longer hostname creates a caution; exact matches and legitimate parent/subdomain relationships remain neutral. Repeated sources/occurrences consolidate without discarding provenance. See [Stage 8 remediation](STAGE8_REMEDIATION_HANDOFF.md).

## Primary selection policy

Invalid input is handled first. Otherwise the display candidates use the following priorities; ties retain the coordinator's deterministic evidence order. These numbers order presentation, not security confidence.

| Priority | Supported finding |
|---|---|
| 110 | Unvalidated hostname, DNS naming error or unreliable original attribution |
| 101 | Explicit Expected Hostname visual resemblance not already explained by the same built-in pair |
| 100 / 99 | Original-host automatic visual resemblance / saved-reference visual resemblance |
| 96 / 95 / 94 | Hidden characters / original userinfo / backslash ambiguity |
| 90 / 89 | Original automatic structural placement / legacy comparison-name placement |
| 85 / 80 / 75 | Embedded visual / embedded structural / other consequential embedded warning |
| 72 / 30 | Explicit hostname mismatch / invalid Expected Hostname |
| 60 / 50 | Malformed percent encoding / unencrypted HTTP cautions |
| 45 / 44 | Original / embedded nondefault port; informational alone |
| 59 / 49 | Embedded encoding / independent HTTP cautions |
| 20 | Spelling-only similarity, informational |
| 10 / 9 / 8 | Explicit exact match / exact saved-reference match / saved-reference subdomain; neutral and qualified |
| fallback | Incomplete checks without meaningful findings; qualified completed negative or compact unsupported-eligibility note |

Ordinary ASCII-character observations are not candidates. Exact popular-domain membership is not a safety endorsement or a positive primary finding. The strongest automatic or embedded resemblance can outrank an exact manual match. The underlying manual comparison and original character assessment remain unchanged; their redundant legacy summary is omitted from the new display. Equivalent same-pair identity evidence is consolidated; distinct sources/proofs remain available. Independent security concerns retain caution treatment: transport evidence is not absorbed into ordinary hostname-identity prose.

An exact saved `example.test` produces “Matches your saved reference”, with the successful hostname comparison explained and unsupported automatic popular-domain comparisons secondary. Saved subdomain and spelling evidence also survive unsupported built-in eligibility. An invalid optional Expected Hostname remains a field/secondary notice when the only other result is a successful saved exact/subdomain comparison. A completed unrelated personal nonmatch is quiet; deliberately opened comparison evidence names the reference. Unavailable visual comparisons and exact-only IP/single-label comparisons have different explanations. Structural labels name the actual matching source; a distinct Expected Hostname must not be substituted. A supported expected visual/structural warning does not repeat a generic mismatch.

For `rnicrosoft.com`, the primary result is “Possible lookalike website”, “May resemble microsoft.com” and the verified rn/m mechanism. A scope label identifies the original address or an address found inside the URL. Finding headings stay short within that context. Resemblance remains possible and font-dependent; nothing establishes malicious intent, ownership or an actual redirect.

During asynchronous preparation the primary headline is hidden. A short separate progress status can appear, rather than a reassuring interim finding. Generation IDs invalidate obsolete work. Processing completion does not move focus. A single polite settled live region uses fixed headlines/coverage and excludes hostnames and private material; the visible primary is not a second live region.

## Universal warning hierarchy and hostname spacing

Priority determines ordering and relative emphasis; it does not remove another independent security finding's caution treatment. The one primary result retains its larger title and three-pixel accent rule. Distinct identity mechanisms for that hostname appear as separate thoughts within it; evidence-appropriate advice appears once per inspection. HTTP-only advice addresses sensitive submissions without HTTPS. Identity cautions direct attention to the actual hostname. Mixed cautions consolidate both recommendations in one advice thought. Neutral and information-only results gain no generic security instruction. Informational spelling, ports, exact matches and ordinary limitations do not turn HTTP-only advice into identity advice.

Independent transport cautions remain separate findings, including HTTP alongside a stronger identity warning. Every secondary `caution` retains the existing two-pixel amber rule and explicit **Caution** label; informational results keep their distinct treatment. Scope is established once for each consecutive run of findings, preserving the exact existing priority order. Labels distinguish **Original address**, **Addresses found inside the URL**, and the optional **Expected Hostname** notice. Each individual finding's accessible name independently includes its scope, severity, descriptive heading and affected hostname, with its explanation referenced separately. The primary group and privacy-safe settled announcement also retain explicit scope. No additional panel is introduced. There are no URL-specific style rules or new confidence classifications.

Security cautions have no three-item display cap. Informational results, including weak spelling suggestions, retain an **Information** label and no amber rule; up to three appear ordinarily, with remaining comparison evidence in Advanced diagnostics. Ordinary unsupported/interrupted coverage notes remain scoped and muted, distinct from security findings. Invalid input, neutral identity/negative results and raw diagnostic severities remain unchanged. HTTP retains security caution treatment. The later stress correction treats nondefault ports proportionately as information when no independent deception evidence applies; original engine diagnostic levels remain unchanged. Malformed percent encoding and recorded embedded transport/hostname-validation cautions are also surfaced. Optional Expected Hostname field errors rank below actual security cautions. Routine preprocessing and matching/extraction coverage remain technical information; no blanket promotion of every raw warn record is used. Technical proof records elaborate existing findings rather than becoming duplicate warning panels.

The shared two-representation identity layout adds 22px before the readable Unicode label, reducing to 20px at the existing 620px breakpoint. Each label retains its seven-pixel association with its own value. Exact browser/Punycode and Unicode values and the existing readable-character cue are unchanged. Only the existing single combined Blackberry & Amethyst palette is used; no separate themes or switch exists.

## Three levels of evidence

The ordinary result has one actual hostname, one primary conclusion/reason/action, all independent secondary cautions plus up to three informational summaries, grouped additional hostnames when useful, and one plain-language limitations location. It omits absent Expected Hostname/personal-reference reports, redundant automatic status panels, neutral membership reports, duplicate normalizations and hypothetical ASCII substitutions. It has a native Technical Details entry only when useful evidence exists, and a direct Advanced diagnostics entry. The two earlier overlapping View buttons are removed.

Technical Details is collapsed by default. Opening it lazily mounts only useful alternate spellings, an explicitly supplied expected hostname, supported comparison records and distinct embedded-host groups. Comparison records show source labels and optional concrete mechanism/boundary evidence. Five records are mounted at a time with deterministic pagination and focus retention. Complete empty modules do not generate filler sections. Readable Unicode/original spellings appear when they explain distinct evidence; case-dependent uppercase-I comparisons explicitly distinguish supplied spelling from native identity.

The manual-acceptance follow-up gives concise Unicode explanations using verified scripts and only differing characters. It omits unchanged intervening text and code-point inventories from ordinary warnings. Individual pairs require independently equal existing skeletons; short verified one-to-many proofs are described as sequences, and ambiguous/missing/long evidence uses a bounded whole-name explanation. Exact code points, official names and full changed spans remain in deliberate Technical Details. Valid distinct Unicode and browser ASCII/Punycode forms appear together; the readable form has a visible script/character cue associated with it through aria-describedby. The cue identifies characters without declaring an internationalized name unsafe. Redundant readable-hostname rows are omitted deeper down.

One visual finding retains every supported Expected Hostname/personal/built-in source for that hostname/reference pair, including independently valid UTS #39 and finite ASCII proofs. Their method names remain distinct. Exact saved membership in the inspected hostname is separate context, never support for a different target's resemblance or a safety endorsement.

Advanced diagnostics is a separate direct deliberate disclosure labeled as potentially containing private URL values. Meaningful independent collapsed categories contain comparison evidence/limits, distinct normalization forms, actual non-ASCII/hidden character evidence, populated URL components, exact embedded occurrences and Raw Diagnostic Records. Equivalent expected/personal proofs share a record with both source labels. Routine complete/suppressed statuses, absent comparisons, empty components, theoretical ASCII inventories and the duplicate legacy assessment/supporting/log presentations are omitted. Precise limitations and built-in rank/row provenance remain in comparison evidence. Generic embedded-format guidance lives in Help. A complete empty extraction produces no report.

Raw Diagnostic Records is the single ordered display of original immutable messages. Further deliberate disclosures retain exhaustive ASCII observations with locations and the original submitted URL. Serialized comparison and attribution objects are not rendered; no diagnostic export is added. Complete per-class coverage, proofs and provenance remain in unchanged result objects and tests, while the interface provides meaningful exceptions, source/method labels, verified character properties and exact occurrence evidence. Exact source values and decoding/parent evidence retain their separate deliberate reveal. Diagnostic subsections already started collapsed; that functioning behavior is preserved.

## Grouping, limits and privacy

Ordinary embedded identity evidence groups by canonical hostname and original/recovered scope: visual/structural evidence and distinct syntax warnings share that identity summary even when secondary. HTTP is a separate transport caution at its existing priority, consolidated per hostname and source scope; repeated occurrences do not create duplicate HTTP warnings. An embedded transport caution names its hostname to identify which recovered address it concerns. Scope labels provide context for short headings such as **Possible lookalike website**, **Unencrypted HTTP**, **Address needs review** and **Port 8080 specified**, avoiding repeated “inside this link” suffixes. Accessible name references preserve essential scope for each individual finding. Unicode/Punycode context appears once per hostname in ordinary findings. Names already shown in primary or visible Other findings are omitted from Also inside this URL; additional distinct names remain there. All groups, occurrences, comparison sources/targets and parent chains remain available through deliberate evidence. Userinfo wording describes the text before @ as outside the actual hostname and makes no claim that sign-in occurred. It reports whether the name differs from the original, a general location and distinct recorded appearance counts. It does not enumerate parent IDs, parameter names, decoding histories, positions or full addresses. Exact entries, parent chains, ranges and source representations remain behind the existing explicit full-value disclosures in advanced diagnostics. A Technical Details button opens/focuses the appropriate exact-occurrence evidence.

Structural ordinary wording uses the supported comparison name: “Having [name] inside this longer hostname does not make it that domain or one of its subdomains.” It applies to automatic and manual placement evidence, original and recovered addresses, without brand or suffix exceptions. Exact registrable boundaries, suffix rules and PRIVATE/ICANN details stay in deliberate Technical Details. Matching policy, eligibility and negative controls are unchanged by this copy refinement.

Completed supported checks with no noteworthy findings show the quiet “No lookalike warnings found” result and one safety qualification. Unsupported-only eligibility instead shows “Automatic comparisons unavailable” and a compact note (for example, .test); it never claims a completed negative. Interrupted execution or unavailable data retains the prominent incomplete-result explanation. Right-to-left visual coverage remains explicitly unsupported even if other comparison classes complete. Complete absence of a supported match is not a safe verdict. Plain-language limitations distinguish unavailable popular-domain checks, unsupported hostname boundaries, incomplete/deeper/encoded embedded addresses, resource limits and incomplete saved/expected comparisons. Related limits consolidate in one ordinary location; exact codes remain in deliberate diagnostics. Positives survive partial checks. The eight-entry value/type cap and every original matching/extraction limit remain unchanged.

Automatic coverage can be aggregate `partial` solely because one hostname completed while another was ineligible. Presentation reads per-analysis states and discovery/occurrence coverage: complete extraction of an embedded `.test` hostname produces an embedded popular-domain eligibility note, not an incomplete-extraction message. Actual interrupted matching, extraction limits and unavailable data retain their separate affected scopes. Equivalent unsupported-suffix notes consolidate; distinct scopes and independent failures survive.

New text uses safe text nodes and `Inspector.visible`. No destination links, inspected-URL persistence, history, telemetry or requests are introduced. Parameter names, credentials, decoded/full values and tokens remain absent from ordinary results, attributes and announcements. Entering advanced diagnostics is an explicit potentially-private action; the further full embedded reveal still controls source values/credentials. Close, reset and reinspection clear mounted sensitive bodies and stale records. A thrown inspection failure also leaves private raw input unmounted until deliberate diagnostic access.

The normal path computes one personal-reference comparison and one extraction, then passes both trusted same-inspection objects into the existing coordinator. Opening diagnostics does not rerun the inspected-URL analysis, extraction or automatic matcher. Index initialization remains scheduled and reused; its previously measured one-time main-thread cost is unchanged. Large diagnostic DOM is generated only on demand. Existing base/v3/embedded CSS, design tokens and reduced-motion rules are preserved; the single combined Blackberry & Amethyst palette remains the approved design.

## Data sources and licenses

Application-level **Data sources & licenses**, outside the per-URL results, retains Unicode notices/license and separate popular-domain/suffix notices. Each legal text is an individually lazy plain-text disclosure. The full MPL text is displayed with real line breaks, not serialized JSON or escaped newline strings. Exact Majestic, PSL, MPL, source-availability and lookalike notices are preserved. Optional Advanced source identities provides source/PSL/index hashes without exposing them in ordinary inspection evidence. No snapshot or licensing text was modified.

## Review and reproduction

```sh
python3 -B tools/build.py --automatic-ui-preview --output-root /private/tmp/oui-stage6-ux-preview
deno task test:ux
python3 -B tests/final-copy-regressions.py --development-root /private/tmp/oui-stage6-ux-preview
```

`test:final-copy`, `test:http-structure`, `test:stress`, `test:prominence`, `test:followup`, `test:acceptance`, `test:messaging`, `test:ux` and `test:automatic-ui` run the current isolated build/message suite; `test:automatic-build` runs current build checks. Use `tests/final-copy-regressions.py` for current copy plus exact historical-interface regressions. Previous assertions, including the former JSON-display, generic-advice and repeated-scope assertions, remain unchanged and run against their matching historical interfaces; they do not define the corrected interface. Exact reversal boundaries and original whole-file pins preserve the historical proof. This presentation-only refinement verifies unchanged strict generator/data/source hashes and preserves the prior successful Deno 2.9.7 report; it does not substitute another runtime or rerun strict generation. No release verifier, public bundle, source snapshot, runtime pin or deployment workflow is changed. See [the final copy review](STAGE6_FINAL_COPY_REVIEW.md).

See [the focused ten-point handoff](STAGE6_UX_REVIEW.md) and [native before/after gallery](STAGE6_UX_BEFORE_AFTER.md). Actual Firefox file and loopback acceptance now includes real 200%/400% tab zoom via a temporary zoom-only helper confined to the disposable test profile. VoiceOver and physical-device acceptance are still unperformed. This remains Stage 6; release hardening and final acceptance are not authorized.

The preceding Stage 6 refinement aligned the offline controls and revised optional-reference help; its evidence remains in [that handoff](STAGE6_FINAL_UX_REVIEW.md). [The preceding messaging review](STAGE6_MESSAGING_REVIEW.md) and [earlier acceptance review](STAGE6_ACCEPTANCE_REVIEW.md) retain their correction and validation evidence. The current refinement is documented in [the HTTP/structure review](STAGE6_HTTP_STRUCTURE_REVIEW.md). [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) holds the standing principles.

The consolidated stress correction removes redundant source-location lines from ordinary recovered findings, retains repeated-occurrence counts, names the actual hostname in userinfo explanations, and uses readable Unicode with a browser/Punycode context for relevant recovered names. Exact source locations remain technical. See STAGE6_STRESS_REVIEW.md for the versioned PRIVATE-tenant structural correction, unchanged input data and strict reproduction.

"""v3.3.0 candidate packaging only. No network, Git mutation or release approval."""
import base64,hashlib,io,json,re,zipfile,platform,zlib
from pathlib import Path
from reference_assets import validate,license_bundle
VERSION='3.3.0-rc.1'
BASELINE='664cc58bf67a2127d0523adec9f1d80c6edd656e'
RUNTIME={'deno':'2.9.7','v8':'15.0.245.2-rusty','typescript':'6.0.3'}
SRC=('automatic-ui.js automatic.css base.css comparisons.js core.js domain-boundaries.js embedded-ui.js embedded.css embedded.js hosted.js lookalikes.js presentation.js reference-data.js references.js results-presentation.js sw.js template.html ui.js v3.css').split()
DATA=('DerivedBidiClass.txt DerivedCoreProperties.txt IdnaMappingTable.txt IdnaTestV2.txt LICENSE.txt NormalizationTest.txt PropertyValueAliases.txt ReadMe.txt ScriptExtensions.txt Scripts.txt UnicodeData.txt confusables.txt manifest.json unicode-data.json unicode-data.sha256 reference-foundation.json lookalikes/NOTICE.txt lookalikes/index.json lookalikes/manifest.json popular-domains/NOTICE.txt popular-domains/provenance.json popular-domains/records.json popular-domains/source.csv popular-domains/source.json public-suffix/LICENSE.txt public-suffix/NOTICE.txt public-suffix/compiled.json public-suffix/public_suffix_list.dat public-suffix/source.json public-suffix/test_psl.txt').split()
TOOLS=('build.py release_candidate.py release_gate.py verify_release.py reference_assets.py extract_majestic.py generate_reference_data.mjs reference_data_lib.mjs generate_lookalike_index.mjs lookalike_data_lib.mjs').split()
DOCS=['REFERENCE_DATA.md','LOOKALIKES.md','COMPARISONS.md','AUTOMATIC_FINDINGS.md','DISTRIBUTION_RIGHTS.md','RELEASE_CANDIDATE.md','deno.json','deno.lock','.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml','tests/stage7-release.py','tests/stage7-regressions.py','tests/stage8-cases.mjs','tests/stage8-results.mjs','tests/stage8-generators.py','tests/stage8-regressions.py']
INPUTS=sorted(['src/'+n for n in SRC]+['data/'+n for n in DATA]+['tools/'+n for n in TOOLS]+DOCS)
ARTIFACTS=['NOTICES.txt','source-materials.zip','site/.nojekyll','site/index.html','site/sw.js','standalone/Offline_URL_Inspector.html']
OUTPUTS=set(ARTIFACTS+['build-manifest.json','SHA256SUMS'])
PSL_SOURCE=['data/public-suffix/public_suffix_list.dat','data/public-suffix/compiled.json','src/domain-boundaries.js','tools/generate_reference_data.mjs','tools/reference_data_lib.mjs']
def sha(raw):return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
def canonical(value):return json.dumps(value,sort_keys=True,separators=(',',':'),ensure_ascii=True)+'\n'
def require(v,message):
    if not v:raise ValueError(message)
def inventory(root):
    result={}
    for name in INPUTS:
        p=root/name
        require(p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink(),'Missing/unsafe candidate input: '+name)
        result[name]={'bytes':p.stat().st_size,'sha256':sha(p.read_bytes())}
    return result

def candidate_licenses(root):
    bundle=license_bundle(root)
    bundle['scope']='Offline URL Inspector 3.3.0 release-candidate data notices. Source material is included offline; this is not release authorization.'
    bundle['sourceAvailability']='The exact preferred Public Suffix List source and its transformed rules follow under MPL 2.0. The transformation program is reproduced for modification/reproduction, with its independently authored modules retaining their existing terms. Complete pinned inputs, notices and build instructions also accompany this candidate in source-materials.zip. No external download is needed to obtain the PSL source.\n'
    for name in PSL_SOURCE:bundle['sourceAvailability']+='\n===== '+name+' =====\n'+(root/name).read_text()
    # Preserve pinned historical notices verbatim, then explain candidate packaging.
    bundle['sourceAvailability']+='\nThe preceding pinned notice describes the earlier development proposal. This candidate supplies the exact sources inline and in its companion archive. See DISTRIBUTION_RIGHTS.md for the engineering assessment and remaining legal review.\n'
    return bundle

def archive_bytes(root):
    output=io.BytesIO()
    with zipfile.ZipFile(output,'w',compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED,compresslevel=9) as archive:
        for name in INPUTS:
            info=zipfile.ZipInfo(name,date_time=(1980,1,1,0,0,0));info.compress_type=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED;info.create_system=3;info.external_attr=0o100644<<16
            archive.writestr(info,(root/name).read_bytes(),compress_type=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED,compresslevel=9)
    return output.getvalue()

def finish(root,out,manifest):
    foundation,_=validate(root);index=json.loads((root/'data/lookalikes/manifest.json').read_text())
    require(index['generator']['runtime']==RUNTIME,'Unapproved index runtime metadata')
    require(set(index['generator']['files'])=={'src/core.js','src/lookalikes.js','tools/generate_lookalike_index.mjs','tools/lookalike_data_lib.mjs'},'Incomplete index generator inventory')
    for name,pin in index['generator']['files'].items():require(sha((root/name).read_bytes())==pin,'Index generator source mismatch: '+name)
    require(foundation['generator']['referenceRuntime']=={'name':'Deno','version':RUNTIME['deno'],'v8':RUNTIME['v8']},'Unapproved foundation runtime metadata')
    require(index['policyId']=='full-domain-conservative-v2' and index['referenceCount']==9570,'Unexpected approved matching policy/count')
    # The data-format stage flags describe their immutable component schemas,
    # not the completed application's feature availability. Never repin them.
    manifest.update(candidateVersion=VERSION,targetVersion='3.3.0',releaseCandidate=True,developmentOnly=True,publicationAuthorized=False,generatorRuntime=RUNTIME)
    manifest['buildToolchain']={'python':platform.python_version(),'zlib':zlib.ZLIB_VERSION,'dependencies':'Python standard library only; no runtime package dependency'}
    inputs=inventory(root)
    manifest['sourceIdentity']={'kind':'sha256-input-inventory','baselineCommit':BASELINE,'inputsSHA256':sha(canonical(inputs).encode()),'inputs':inputs,'meaning':'Content identity of explicitly enumerated candidate inputs; not an immutable Git commit or independent audit approval.'}
    manifest['datasets']={'majesticOriginal':foundation['source']['original'],'majesticSubset':foundation['source']['subset'],'psl':foundation['psl'],'foundationSHA256':sha((root/'data/reference-foundation.json').read_bytes()),'indexSHA256':index['index']['sha256'],'matchingPolicy':index['policyId'],'unicodeSHA256':foundation['unicode']['sha256']}
    (out/'source-materials.zip').write_bytes(archive_bytes(root))
    notices='Offline URL Inspector '+VERSION+' — third-party data notices\n\n'
    for name in ['data/LICENSE.txt','data/popular-domains/NOTICE.txt','data/public-suffix/NOTICE.txt','data/public-suffix/LICENSE.txt','data/lookalikes/NOTICE.txt','DISTRIBUTION_RIGHTS.md']:
        notices+='\n===== '+name+' =====\n'+(root/name).read_text()
    notices+='\nExact preferred PSL source and modifications are included in both HTML editions under Data sources & licenses and in source-materials.zip. Distribute the complete candidate bundle; an HTML file also retains these notices and PSL source offline.\n'
    (out/'NOTICES.txt').write_text(notices)
    actual={str(p.relative_to(out)) for p in out.rglob('*') if p.is_file()}
    require(actual==set(ARTIFACTS),'Unexpected or stale files in candidate output: '+str(actual.symmetric_difference(ARTIFACTS)))
    manifest['artifacts']={name:{'sha256':sha((out/name).read_bytes()),'bytes':(out/name).stat().st_size} for name in ARTIFACTS}
    manifest['distribution']={'hostedInputs':['site/index.html','site/sw.js','site/.nojekyll'],'standalone':'standalone/Offline_URL_Inspector.html','sourceAndNotices':['source-materials.zip','NOTICES.txt'],'excluded':'Tests, reports, screenshots, previews, full-million CSV, credentials, Git/editor metadata, historical site/standalone outputs. Source archive contains only the explicit input allowlist.'}
    # build.py writes this exact manifest once more after returning.
    (out/'build-manifest.json').write_text(json.dumps(manifest,indent=2)+'\n')
    (out/'SHA256SUMS').write_text(''.join(sha((out/name).read_bytes())+'  '+name+'\n' for name in sorted(OUTPUTS-{'SHA256SUMS'})))

def verify(root,out,*,rebuild=True):
    root=Path(root).resolve();out=Path(out).resolve()
    require(out!=root and root not in out.parents,'Candidate must be outside the source repository')
    actual={str(p.relative_to(out)) for p in out.rglob('*') if p.is_file() or p.is_symlink()}
    require(actual==OUTPUTS,'Distribution inventory mismatch')
    require(not any(p.is_symlink() for p in out.rglob('*')),'Symlink in candidate')
    m=json.loads((out/'build-manifest.json').read_text())
    require(m.get('candidateVersion')==VERSION and m.get('releaseCandidate') is True and m.get('publicationAuthorized') is False,'Incorrect candidate version/status')
    require(m.get('generatorRuntime')==RUNTIME,'Incorrect generator runtime')
    require(m['sourceIdentity']['inputs']==inventory(root),'Candidate source input identity mismatch')
    require(m['sourceIdentity']['inputsSHA256']==sha(canonical(inventory(root)).encode()),'Candidate source digest mismatch')
    require(set(m['artifacts'])==set(ARTIFACTS),'Incomplete artifact manifest')
    require(m['release']==VERSION+'-'+m['hosted']['sha256'][:16],'Incorrect release identity')
    lines=(out/'SHA256SUMS').read_text().splitlines();entries={}
    for line in lines:
        digest,name=line.split('  ',1)
        require(name in OUTPUTS-{'SHA256SUMS'} and name not in entries,'Unexpected/duplicate checksum entry')
        require(sha((out/name).read_bytes())==digest,'Artifact checksum mismatch: '+name);entries[name]=digest
    require(set(entries)==OUTPUTS-{'SHA256SUMS'},'Incomplete checksum inventory')
    for name,item in m['artifacts'].items():require(item=={'sha256':sha((out/name).read_bytes()),'bytes':(out/name).stat().st_size},'Artifact manifest mismatch: '+name)
    for edition,name in [('standalone','standalone/Offline_URL_Inspector.html'),('hosted','site/index.html')]:
        html=(out/name).read_text();require('Version '+VERSION in html,'Incorrect visible application version')
        require(sha((out/name).read_bytes())==m[edition]['sha256'],'Edition manifest mismatch')
        for tag,key in [('script','scriptHash'),('style','styleHash')]:
            matches=re.findall('<'+tag+'>([\\s\\S]*?)</'+tag+'>',html)
            require(len(matches)==1,'Unexpected executable/style block inventory')
            digest=base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha256(matches[0].encode()).digest()).decode()
            require(digest==m[edition][key] and tag+"-src 'sha256-"+digest+"'" in html,'CSP hash mismatch')
        for directive in ["default-src 'none'","connect-src 'none'","base-uri 'none'","form-action 'none'","img-src 'none'","object-src 'none'","frame-src 'none'"]:
            require(directive in html,'Missing CSP directive')
        require('unsafe-inline' not in html and 'unsafe-eval' not in html,'Unsafe CSP')
        require(not re.search(r'<(?:script|link|img)\b[^>]*(?:src|href)\s*=',html,re.I),'External runtime dependency')
        legal=json.loads(re.search(r'id="reference-licenses">([\s\S]*?)</script>',html).group(1))
        require(legal==candidate_licenses(root),'Missing or stale offline notices/source materials')
    # Rebuild from the identified sources. This compares every byte, including
    # CSP, inert data, full legal/source material, worker and both manifests.
    if rebuild:
        import subprocess,tempfile
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='oui-rc-verify-') as folder:
            p=subprocess.run(['python3','-B',str(root/'tools/build.py'),'--release-candidate','--output-root',folder],cwd=root,capture_output=True,text=True)
            require(p.returncode==0,'Candidate rebuild failed: '+p.stderr[-4000:])
            for name in sorted(OUTPUTS):require((out/name).read_bytes()==(Path(folder)/name).read_bytes(),'Source-to-artifact mismatch: '+name)
    return {'version':VERSION,'release':m['release'],'sourceInputsSHA256':m['sourceIdentity']['inputsSHA256'],'filesVerified':len(OUTPUTS),'sourceCorrespondenceRebuilt':rebuild,'publicationAuthorized':False}

name: Verify and explicitly deploy URL Inspector

# No automatic push deployment. Future dispatch requires an exact reviewed
# commit on main, an accepted source digest and explicit authorization.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      candidate_commit:
        description: Exact audited 40-character main commit
        required: true
        type: string
      source_inputs_sha256:
        description: Accepted candidate input digest from its build manifest
        required: true
        type: string
      authorize_deployment:
        description: Stage 8 accepted and deployment explicitly authorized
        required: true
        default: false
        type: boolean

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.authorize_deployment
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Bind dispatch to the checked-out immutable commit
        env:
          EXPECTED_COMMIT: ${{ inputs.candidate_commit }}
        run: |
          test "$EXPECTED_COMMIT" = "$GITHUB_SHA"
          test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$GITHUB_SHA"
      - name: Install isolated checksum-pinned official Deno 2.9.7
        run: |
          mkdir "$RUNNER_TEMP/deno-runtime"
          curl --fail --location --max-time 120 --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 https://github.com/denoland/deno/releases/download/v2.9.7/deno-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.zip -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/deno-runtime/deno.zip"
          echo 'c6527f24f4b16031d3ae4fa9f658d5f11534c8d84ce7dc8502420280919c3490  '"$RUNNER_TEMP/deno-runtime/deno.zip" | sha256sum --check --strict
          unzip -j "$RUNNER_TEMP/deno-runtime/deno.zip" deno -d "$RUNNER_TEMP/deno-runtime"
          chmod 700 "$RUNNER_TEMP/deno-runtime/deno"
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/deno-runtime" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: Cache only locked development dependencies
        run: deno cache --frozen --lock=deno.lock tests/final-copy-results.mjs
      - name: Build exact candidate and verify prerequisites
        env:
          EXPECTED_SOURCE: ${{ inputs.source_inputs_sha256 }}
        run: |
          python3 -B tools/build.py --release-candidate --output-root "$RUNNER_TEMP/rc"
          python3 -B tools/verify_release.py --candidate-root "$RUNNER_TEMP/rc"
          python3 -B tools/release_gate.py --candidate-root "$RUNNER_TEMP/rc" --deno "$(command -v deno)" --report "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-gate.json"
          python3 -c 'import json,os; m=json.load(open(os.environ["RUNNER_TEMP"]+"/rc/build-manifest.json")); assert m["sourceIdentity"]["inputsSHA256"]==os.environ["EXPECTED_SOURCE"], "Unreviewed source inputs"'
      - name: Preserve historical regression contracts
        run: python3 -B tests/stage8-regressions.py --candidate-root "$RUNNER_TEMP/rc" --report "$RUNNER_TEMP/historical-results.json"
      - name: Preserve candidate identity and verification receipt
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: verified-candidate-${{ github.sha }}
          path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/rc/build-manifest.json
            ${{ runner.temp }}/rc/SHA256SUMS
            ${{ runner.temp }}/release-gate.json
            ${{ runner.temp }}/historical-results.json
          if-no-files-found: error
      - name: Upload only the newly verified hosted edition
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@7b1f4a764d45c48632c6b24a0339c27f5614fb0b # v4
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/rc/site
          include-hidden-files: true
  deploy:
    needs: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Reject a run superseded while awaiting approval
        run: test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$GITHUB_SHA"
      - name: Deploy this run's verified artifact
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@d6db90164ac5ed86f2b6aed7e0febac5b3c0c03e # v4
